subject.title: iOS app: node requests re-approval on every reconnect (token persistence bug)

question: Is the merged LAN bootstrap persistence fix sufficient to close this issue, or should this stay open until a current-main iOS LAN/VPN reconnect proof rules out remaining permission/capability reapproval drift?
rationale: The code proves one related auth-token loss path is fixed, but current source still has legitimate reapproval triggers that could match the reporter's repeated reconnect symptom.

options.title: Keep for live iOS proof
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main iPhone reconnect run that distinguishes token loss from capability or permission-surface reapproval before closing.

options.title: Close as covered by LAN token fix
options.body: Close if an iOS owner accepts the source regression as sufficient proof that the reporter's repeated reapproval was only the fixed bootstrap handoff bug.

options.title: Split security-surface follow-up
options.body: Close the token-persistence portion and open a narrower owner issue for dynamic iOS permission/capability reapproval if live proof confirms that is the remaining cause.

recommendation.title: Keep for live iOS proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main iPhone reconnect run that distinguishes token loss from capability or permission-surface reapproval before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent iOS/gateway auth work and the LAN bootstrap regression consolidation make this the best available routing owner for the proof-sufficiency call.
